questions.stem: To solve $3x + 2y = 12$ and $5x + 2y = 20$ by elimination, what should you do first?

options.text: Subtract one equation from the other to eliminate $y$

questions.explanation: Since both equations have $2y$, subtracting one from the other eliminates $y$ immediately: $(5x + 2y) - (3x + 2y) = 20 - 12$, giving $2x = 8$.
Multiply eq 2 by 2: $2x + 4y = 16$. Subtract from eq 1: $(3x + 4y) - (2x + 4y) = 18 - 16$, giving $x = 2$. Substitute: $2 + 2y = 8$, so $y = 3$.
Multiply eq 2 by 3: $12x - 3y = 15$. Add to eq 1: $14x = 28$, so $x = 2$. Substitute: $4 + 3y = 13$, so $y = 3$.

questions.stem: When should you add equations rather than subtract them?

options.text: When the coefficients of the variable to eliminate have the same sign
When the coefficients of the variable to eliminate have opposite signs

questions.explanation: Add the equations when the coefficients have opposite signs (e.g., $+3y$ and $-3y$), as adding will eliminate that variable. Subtract when they have the same sign.

questions.stem: After solving a pair of simultaneous equations, how should you check your answer?

options.text: Substitute the values into the first equation only
Substitute the values into both original equations to verify they are satisfied
Check that neither value is negative

questions.explanation: Always substitute your values back into both original equations. If both are satisfied, your solution is correct.
